doc.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Principles, injustice and a life given to music
summary: Hampton on justice and integrity, hating selfishness, and knowing from first hearing that music was his path.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: I was already that way, and my son is the same way. He’s the same way. He’s against injustice to the teeth. He’s against somebody doing something unfair to somebody else. This just really bothers him. I was always that way. Somebody doing something that was unfair to someone else always really just turned me off. Justice and principle and integrity was something that was always important to me. If I can have that, I can stand everything else that I have to go through. I don’t want any of the luxuries without having those things. Those are the things that were important to me. Those are the things that are important to me, is that when I get something, I get it by doing hard work for it, being fair to get it, being fair to people, and being concerned about other people that might be in a situation that I might have been in, or I might be in. Those are the things that are important to me. Selfishness is a thing that I hate. I hate selfishness. I know some people that are good musicians that are very selfish. I don’t like it. There’s no need for me to lie.
So there really is no end to your education.

We can’t say that in – I guess, in 1944, you were, what? 12 years old – we can’t say that in 1948, you crossed some boundary called high school and went to something else. You, from as long as you can remember, were being shaped to be a musician.
Once I heard music, I knew that’s what I’m going to do. I’m going to learn about this.
And from the time you were 3 or 4 years old, until now, at one point or another you have been a performer.

I’ve been at least wanting to learn about music. I’ve loved music from the very beginning. I’ve loved the fact that music would take me to places that most other work wouldn’t take me. I knew that music would take me to places that I could meet people that were different than me and people that had a different background than me, and I knew that that would be a place that I could learn something.
